text:
Alyssa: quick check — we're still split on whether to go with a typed-bridge (protobuf/gRPC inside, JSON at edge) or a smart-forwarder (JSON everywhere, runtime type checks + schema registry). Thoughts on operational surface and console signals we should care about?

Devon: I prefer typed-bridge for internal services. clear contracts, easier to validate backward compatibility. but it adds a gateway layer that we need to own.

Samir: typed-bridge gives us better perf for long-running streams (gRPC). however the gateway will need header mapping for quotas and tracing. avoid magic transcodes that drop x-customer-id.

Jordan: smart-forwarder wins for rollout speed — no proto codegen step for product teams. but we lose strictness; debugging contract drift is harder. console would need schema-diff telemetry.

Alyssa: good points. operational concerns: 1) quota enforcement fidelity (per-tenant limits must not be flattened during translation) 2) route-level latency attribution in console 3) canary rollout signals — how to show contract errors in the UI

Maria: suggestion: hybrid pattern — typed-bridge for core infra paths (routing, billing, kv-heavy RPCs) and smart-forwarder for low-risk public endpoints. expose a "contract mismatch" trace span in console when translation fails.

Devon: +1 hybrid. For typed-bridge we should emit two traces: upstream-proto and downstream-json with correlation id. that makes latency slices clear in the console timeline. also a small histogram for proto->json encode time.

Samir: quotas: keep authoritative quota check after the bridge, not before. otherwise a stale JSON header could let requests bypass. so gateway must fetch /quota/validate proto call (fast cache allowed). console shows quota-hit vs throttle reasons.

Jordan: rollout UX: add a console toggle per-route: proto_mode = [off, permissive, strict]. permissive logs contract errors (metrics + slowlog) but accepts request. strict rejects. start permissive in canary.

Alyssa: I like that. Implementation checklist: 
- gate toggle in console per-route (string)
- bridge emits contract-error metric + sample payload to s3 for later diffs
- trace spans for encode/decode and quota-check RPCs
- header mapping table (explicit mapping list) and linting pre-deploy
- test harness that fuzzes proto<->json translations

Maria: ops-bot note: deploy bot will add a warning to PRs that touch gateway header mappings. sample lint rule: if you remove a header mapping, you must add migration note.

ops-bot: Reminder: tomorrow 11:30am sync for gateway rollout. Agenda: toggle design, telemetry schemas, canary plan.

Samir: one last thing — keep an exportable contract snapshot per release so we can blame/regress when customer regressions show up. store alongside release artifacts.

Alyssa: OK lets move forward with hybrid. I'll draft an RFC with the toggle UX and the telemetry schema (contract_error metric, span names, encode histo). tagging folks for review. thanks all.
